text: Axitinib, marketed under the brand name Inlyta, is a small molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitor developed by Pfizer. It has demonstrated significant inhibition of breast cancer growth in animal xenograft models and has shown partial responses in clinical trials for renal cell carcinoma (RCC) and other tumor types. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved axitinib for the treatment of RCC after it demonstrated a modest increase in progression-free survival, although fatal adverse effects have been reported. Approval for RCC was granted by the FDA in January 2012, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) in September 2012, the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) in September 2012, and the Australian Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) in July 2012. A Phase II trial indicated good response when axitinib was combined with gemcitabine for advanced pancreatic cancer, but Pfizer halted a Phase III trial on 30 January 2009 due to lack of improved survival compared to gemcitabine alone. A 2010 Phase III trial for previously treated metastatic RCC showed significantly extended progression-free survival compared to sorafenib, leading the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) to unanimously recommend FDA approval in December 2011 for axitinib as second-line treatment for advanced RCC. Axitinib has also been studied in combination with the ALK1 inhibitor dalantercept. A 2015 study showed that axitinib effectively inhibits the BCR-ABL1[T315I] mutated gene, common in drug-resistant chronic myeloid leukemia and adult acute lymphoblastic leukemia, representing one of the first instances of a new indication for an existing drug discovered through screening patient cells. Common side effects include diarrhea, hypertension, fatigue, decreased appetite, nausea, dysphonia, hand-foot syndrome, weight loss, vomiting, asthenia, and constipation, occurring in more than 20% of patients. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4/CYP3A5 inhibitors or inducers should be avoided due to potential increases or decreases in axitinib plasma exposure. Its primary mechanism of action involves inhibition of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 1–3, c-KIT, and PDGFR, thereby suppressing angiogenesis in tumors; it may also induce autophagy, similar to sorafenib. Axitinib has been shown to bind to the BCR-ABL fusion protein in a conformation distinct from VEGF binding, specifically inhibiting the drug-resistant T315I mutant isoform. In July 2024, the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use adopted a positive opinion recommending marketing authorization for Axitinib Accord, developed by Accord Healthcare S.L.U., for the treatment of adults with RCC. Pfizer reported US$1.036 billion in revenue for Inlyta in 2023. In the European Union, axitinib is sold under the brand name Inlyta.
